record.paper_title: AUTOMORPHISMS AND DYNAMICS: A LIST OF OPEN PROBLEMS
record.context_brief: Realizability of linear groups as automorphism groups
record.original_question: Let n ≥ 2. Which subgroups Γ of GL_n(Z) can occur as the discrete automorphism group of a projective variety? More precisely: when is Γ abstractly realizable, meaning that there exists a projective variety X whose automorphism group Aut(X) is isomorphic to Γ as an abstract group; and when is Γ strongly realizable, meaning that there exists a smooth complex projective variety X and a Z-defined linear algebraic representation φ: GL_m(R) → GL(H^2(X; R)) such that the discrete cohomological action Aut(X)^* coincides with φ(Γ)? In particular, is every finitely generated subgroup Γ ⊂ GL_n(Z) abstractly realizable, or strongly realizable, as a group of automorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. Which subgroups of GLn(Z) are abstractly (resp. strongly) realizable as groups of automorphisms ? Is every finitely generated subgroup Γ ⊂ GLn(Z) abstractly (resp. strongly) realizable as a group of automorphisms ?

say that a group Γ is abstractly realizable as a group of automorphisms (in dimension d) if there exist a projective variety X (of dimension d) such that Aut(X) is isomorphic to Γ (as abstract groups).

Say that a group Γ ⊂ GLm(Z) is strongly realizable as a group of automorphisms if there is a smooth complex projective variety X, and a linear algebraic representation ϕ: GLm(R) → GL(H2(X; R)) which is defined over Z, such that Aut(X)∗ coincides with ϕ(Γ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 2. For a complex projective variety X, let Aut(X) denote its group of automorphisms (as an algebraic variety), and for X smooth let Aut(X)* denote the image of Aut(X) acting on the second cohomology H^2(X;R) by pullback.

Call a group Γ abstractly realizable as a group of automorphisms (in dimension d) if there exists a projective variety X (of dimension d) such that Aut(X) is isomorphic to Γ as an abstract group.

Call a subgroup Γ ⊂ GL_m(Z) strongly realizable as a group of automorphisms if there exist a smooth complex projective variety X and a Z-defined linear algebraic representation φ: GL_m(R) → GL(H^2(X;R)) such that Aut(X)* = φ(Γ).

Determine which subgroups Γ ⊂ GL_n(Z) are abstractly realizable, and which are strongly realizable, as groups of automorphisms. In particular, decide whether every finitely generated subgroup Γ ⊂ GL_n(Z) is abstractly realizable (respectively, strongly realizable) as a group of automorphisms.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of characterizing which subgroups of GL_n(Z) arise as automorphism groups of projective varieties (in either the abstract or strong sense) appears in a list of open problems on automorphisms and dynamics. Related results exist for abelian varieties as automorphism groups and examples of discrete non-finitely generated automorphism groups, but no general classification or affirmative/negative answer to the realizability question for arbitrary finitely generated subgroups of GL_n(Z) was found.

status_evidence.title: A projective variety with discrete, non-finitely generated automorphism group
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs projective varieties with discrete, non-finitely generated automorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist but do not classify realizable subgroups of GL_n(Z).

status_evidence.title: Abelian varieties as automorphism groups of smooth projective varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Realizes abelian varieties as automorphism groups of smooth projective varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial realizability results are available; the general GL_n(Z) question remains.

status_evidence.title: Notes on automorphism groups of projective varieties (Brion)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of automorphism groups of projective varieties.
status_evidence.claim: No classification of realizable subgroups of GL_n(Z) is given.
